description: Route the four cam worker spawns (implementer, reviewer, planner, auditor) into the long-lived cam-worker Docker container via a shared dockerExecWrap chokepoint, gated on a fail-closed [loop] worker_isolation flag (default host), with no host fallback.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: docker exec runs the trailing command exec'd directly as argv, NOT through a shell (a chained/quoted command needs an explicit `sh -c`). Since the host tmux pane shell tokenizes the wrapped string, `docker exec -it cam-worker env -u CLAUDECODE ... claude ... '<prompt>'` passes env/claude/prompt as argv with no inner sh -c needed. `-it` (interactive + pseudo-TTY) works and is the standard pattern; the pane is the controlling PTY. No breaking changes or deprecations in current versions.

userStories.title: Add fail-closed [loop] worker_isolation config reader
userStories.description: As the sidecar, I need a config flag that says whether workers spawn on the host or inside the container so that container routing is opt-in and a typo can never silently disable the sandbox.
acceptanceCriteria: readWorkerIsolation reads [loop] worker_isolation from project.toml and returns 'container' only when the value is exactly "container"; every other case (missing file, missing [loop] section, missing key, malformed TOML, non-string, or any other value) fail-closes to 'host'. [oracle: bun test]

The reader accepts a configPath override (DI) so tests target a tmp fixture without mutating scripts/cam/project.toml; a fixture with worker_isolation="container" returns 'container', a fixture with worker_isolation="bogus" returns 'host'. [oracle: bun test]
A WorkerIsolation type ('host' | 'container') is exported from src/config/models.ts alongside MetaLoop/PlanApproval. [oracle: grep -q 'WorkerIsolation' src/config/models.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
bun run check:all passes. [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Mirror readMetaLoop (src/config/models.ts:227) and readPlanApproval (:258) exactly: same try/catch, same [loop] section lookup, same fail-closed default. The [loop] section already exists (meta_loop lives there). Default 'host' is the fail-closed default per the CAM-139 hard-precondition alignment (container active == flag on + preflight ready). userStories.title: Add dockerExecWrap() shared chokepoint helper
userStories.description: As the four dispatch sites, I need one shared helper that wraps an existing worker shell string in `docker exec -it cam-worker ...` so that the container routing lives in a single tested place instead of being duplicated across loop.ts, review.ts and plan-runner.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: dockerExecWrap(shellString, containerName?) returns 'docker exec -it <containerName> ' + shellString with the inner string unchanged; the default containerName is DEFAULT_CONTAINER_NAME ('cam-worker') imported from worker-container.ts (no duplicate literal). [oracle: bun test]

The inner shell string is preserved byte-for-byte, so the CAM-43 env -u prefix, CAM-23 lowercase --session-id, --model quoting and the single-quoted prompt run INSIDE the container. [oracle: bun test]
An argv-shape test asserts the wrapped output begins with 'docker exec -it cam-worker env -u CLAUDECODE ' and still contains ' claude ' after the env prefix. [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
bun run check:all passes. [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: New file src/supervisor/docker-exec.ts: pure function, no I/O (same discipline as worker-argv.ts / plan-argv.ts). env -u must run INSIDE the container, which it does because the wrap prepends 'docker exec -it cam-worker ' to the existing 'env -u ... claude ...' string. Per the fetched Docker exec reference: docker exec execs argv directly (no shell), and the host pane shell tokenizes the wrapped string, so NO inner sh -c is needed. Reuse DEFAULT_CONTAINER_NAME from src/supervisor/worker-container.ts. Test under test/supervisor/. patterns.md: 'tmux mangles TAB' and single-hub dispatch are unaffected (send-keys targets the host pane, unchanged).

userStories.title: Ensure-up idempotent container lifecycle at supervisor boot
userStories.description: As the sidecar boot path, I need to reconcile the cam-worker container to a ready state before dispatching so that container mode has a live long-lived container to exec into, reused across dispatches and sessions.
acceptanceCriteria: ensureWorkerContainer reconciles container state idempotently across four branches: running->reuse (no-op), stopped->docker start, absent->build+run (runWorkerContainer), image-stale->rebuild+recreate (docker rm -f + runWorkerContainer); each branch is DI-tested with an injected spawnFn/probe and never touches a real daemon. [oracle: bun test]

Reconciliation reuses runWorkerContainer (build+run) and preflightWorkerContainer (image-stale detection) instead of duplicating docker argv. [oracle: grep -q 'runWorkerContainer' src/supervisor/ensure-container.ts]
Ensure-up runs only when worker_isolation=container; in host mode it is a no-op with zero docker calls. [oracle: bun test]
cam stop does NOT tear down the container: stop.ts contains no docker stop/rm call, so the container is reusable across sessions. [oracle: grep -c docker src/commands/stop.ts prints 0]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
bun run check:all passes. [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: New file src/supervisor/ensure-container.ts; wire it at sidecar boot in src/commands/sidecar.ts near buildSupervisorOptions. Gate on readWorkerIsolation()==='container' (US-001). Reuse ContainerSpawnFn/DockerProbe seams already exported by worker-container.ts and preflight-container.ts; probe container state via `docker inspect -f {{.State.Running}} cam-worker` (missing container => absent, exit non-zero). Spec gotcha: cam stop must NOT drop the container (only SIGTERMs the tmux session); a dedicated reset command is out of scope. File-size: sidecar.ts is at 1090 ceiling; if the boot wiring exceeds it, raise scripts/file-size-budget.json with a CAM-152 _ref and stage it before check:all (patterns.md 'Ratchet gate').

userStories.title: Flip the implementer spawn through the container (fail-closed) + ADR
userStories.description: As the sidecar implement loop, I need the implementer worker to spawn inside the container in container mode and to fail closed when the container is not ready so that autonomous code-writing runs are sandboxed with no silent host fallback.
acceptanceCriteria: With worker_isolation=container the loop.ts implementer dispatch wraps shellCmd via dockerExecWrap before the respawn-pane -k (loop.ts ~825); with worker_isolation=host the shellCmd is passed unchanged. [oracle: bun test]

preflightContainerFn is flipped from observe-only to fail-closed in container mode: when preflight returns ready:false the loop escalates via escalateFn and returns { status: 'blocked' } with a reason naming the container failure; it NEVER respawns an un-wrapped host worker. [oracle: bun test]
A runtime docker-exec failure (container gone mid-dispatch) routes to a blocked terminal with a container-named reason and no host fallback path. [oracle: bun test]

Invariants preserved through the wrap: an argv-shape test asserts the dispatched string is 'docker exec -it cam-worker env -u CLAUDECODE ... claude ... --session-id <lowercase-uuid> ...' and that host-pane send-keys and the mutex-1-worker-pane are unchanged. [oracle: bun test]
In host mode (default) every existing loop test passes byte-for-byte (zero behavior change). [oracle: bun test]

An ADR records the worker-isolation flip: opt-in flag default-host, fail-closed with no host fallback, one long-lived reusable container (extend docs/adr/0003 or add docs/adr/0007). [oracle: grep -rq 'fail-closed' docs/adr/]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
bun run check:all passes. [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: loop.ts implement branch ~755-825 builds shellCmd from buildImplementerWorkerArgv then respawn-pane -k. The preflightContainerFn seam at ~796-810 is currently observe-only (its comment already says 'B-2 (CAM-152) will flip this fail-closed using escalateFn'). host.ts buildSupervisorOptions (~561/649) wires preflightContainerFn + escalateFn today and must now read readWorkerIsolation() and thread the mode into opts. Reuse the existing escalateFn (loop.ts ~1266) and blocked-return idiom (loop.ts ~925/947). Fail-closed is LITERAL: do not add any host fallback path (spec + CAM-139 safety-net rationale). ADR 0003 already forward-references CAM-152; extend it rather than restate. File-size: loop.ts (1669) and host.ts (696) are at ceiling; raise scripts/file-size-budget.json with a CAM-152 _ref if exceeded (ratchet gate).
